description: Aetrova: a solo build for the CLPS Lunar Mission Browser. A mission-control dashboard for the Moon's south pole: compare landing sites and dates, see sunlight for power and line of sight to Earth's ground stations in a 360° horizon view, plus eclipses, signal delay and past missions. Built on real NASA and ISRO data (LOLA, Diviner, Chandrayaan-2/3), checked against NASA SPICE, with uncertainty shown. Three.js, React, Python, Supabase.
summary: Aetrova is a browser-based simulation of power and communications at the Moon's south pole, built for the CLPS Lunar Mission Browser challenge. One simulation clock drives everything: the terrain horizon built from NASA LRO LOLA elevation data, the Sun's position and disc (so ridges give partial sunlight, and eclipses are handled), estimated solar power with a 48-hour battery simulation, and Earth contact with the Goldstone, Madrid and Canberra stations, including light time, path loss, link margin and Doppler. Users scrub time or change playback speed and watch sunlight, power and link status change together at predefined mission sites, including Chandrayaan-3 context. At the pole the Sun skims the horizon, so a site can lose light and signal at once; planners need one timeline that shows both. Every panel is labeled Computed, Modeled or Context, so it is clear what is physics and what is an assumption. This is a technical demonstrator, not a flight-certified system.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Aetrova simulates sunlight, power and Earth contact at lunar south-pole sites on one live clock. Users change the simulation time and speed and see terrain, Sun elevation, eclipse state, estimated solar watts, a 48-hour battery simulation, and the link to Earth's ground stations update together. Panels cover terrain, timeline, telemetry, power, Earth contact, environment, relay and missions.

HOW IT WORKS (all in the browser, static Next.js export, no server or database)

- Terrain horizon masks computed from NASA LRO LOLA elevation data in a Web Worker.

- Sun and Earth positions from astronomy-engine, with the Sun as a disc (partial sunlight on ridges) and eclipse handling.

- Earth contact: visibility from the local terrain horizon to Goldstone, Madrid and Canberra, with a station-side Moon keep-out; one-way light time, path loss, link margin and Doppler.

- Power: live solar watts, load, state of charge and a 48-hour battery simulation.

- Context: predefined mission sites including Chandrayaan-3, and NASA Moon Trek WMTS map layers.

EVIDENCE LEVELS

Each panel is labeled COMPUTED (physics from data), MODELED (our assumptions: relay orbits, region sampling, simplified gravity field, power model) or CONTEXT (map layers, mission records).

TESTING AND VALIDATION

Unit tests cover frame transforms, light time, Sun disc, eclipses, link and power calculations. Validation against NASA SPICE is in progress.

WALKTHROUGH VIDEO (4 min):Video Project 4.mp4 - Google Drive

LIMITATIONS

A technical demonstrator, not a flight-certified system. Power results are demo-model outputs, not hardware efficiency. Click-anywhere horizon and relay-satellite orbits are next steps.

TOOLS

Next.js, React, TypeScript, three.js with React Three Fiber, Zustand, astronomy-engine, Comlink.

WHY IT MATTERS

At the pole the Sun skims the horizon, so a site can lose power and communications together. Planners need one timeline that shows both.
